page: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Dldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64 and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance is bundled with a 945 GB local disk and is Premium Storage capable. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2163.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.37 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is characterized as average, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 13256.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 15986.98. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), support specialized workloads. This is reflected in the top-tier text generation speed of 396.44 tokens per second for a small 135M parameter LLM, though performance scales down to an average of 15.67 tokens per second for a medium 7B model. Memory bandwidth is measured at 1240.45 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 125.11 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D16lds_v6 offers a resource-dense configuration for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a clear tradeoff, making it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or massive data-science datasets, but highly efficient for raw CPU processing. The inclusion of a 945 GB local disk provides high-speed temporary storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for intermediate files. This server is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, text processing, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference.
